predicted: pFedMe lambda sweep, queued 2026-08-24 after prediction 3 FAILED as stated. The prediction was that pFedMe's personalised model beats its own global model on EVERY pool; at the default lam=15 it does so on 2 of 4, and the mean advantage of +0.0002 AUPRC was carried by one pool. The prediction said a failure would mean our implementation is wrong. On inspection it means something else, and the distinction matters: at lam=15 the inner proximal step is lr/(1+lam) ~ 0.03, so across five local epochs the personalised model barely departs from the global one. pFedMe was being run in a configuration that cannot express its own idea. That is not a refutation of pFedMe, it is a straw man, and it is ours. Our adaptive shrinkage selects its interpolation weight on held-out data. A competitor whose corresponding knob is pinned at an arbitrary value is not a fair comparator, so pFedMe now gets lam in {1, 5, 50} beside the existing 15. PREDICTIONS. (1) The personalisation gain grows as lambda falls, because a weaker proximal pull lets the personalised model move further from the global one; at lam=1 it should beat its global on most or all pools. (2) At lam=50 personalisation is essentially nil and pFedMe reduces to its aggregation behaviour. (3) Even at its best lambda, pFedMe's DEPLOYED model does not beat adaptive shrinkage on mean share above the attainable-gain floor -- our arm selects its weight on data while pFedMe's is fixed per run, and selection is worth more here than the functional form, which is what Result 106 measured. WITHDRAWAL: if pFedMe at any swept lambda beats adaptive shrinkage on mean share above the floor, the recommendation in section 6 is wrong as stated and must be rewritten around whichever arm wins, with the sweep disclosed -- including that pFedMe was given a sweep our own arm was not.
